body:
# Independent audit: logarithmic cap load and quadratic reserve

Source: `candidate 3432196fb93eb580`.

**Full Sections 1–5 PASS.** No substantive correction requested.
This audit rederives the analytic steps rather than relying on the earlier
Slab audit.

* Off the zero set, uniform (L_j\)-convergence gives uniform convergence
  of every bounded logarithmic truncation. Exhaustion identifies the
  ordinary parts of both positive measures. Because the limiting boundary
  measure gives the zero set mass zero, the residual restrictions there
  are nonnegative and satisfy (0\le a\le b\).

* The allowed test ((\ell_j-1)_+\), together with the positive sign of
  the (\lambda_j\ell_j\) term, bounds
  \(\lambda_j\int\ell_{j,+}^2\). The scalar inequality
  \(s^2\le s(s-1)_++s\) has the correct direction. A bounded sequence
  \(\beta_j\) suffices for this estimate; in the actual application
  \(0\le\beta_j\le1\), as used in its displayed constant. The resulting
  nonnegative reserve is supported on the zero set.

* On (a,b>0\), the Hessian of (a\log(a/b)\) is positive semidefinite
  of rank one. After subtracting (Ta\) and taking the maximum with zero,
  the function is increasing in its first coordinate and decreasing in
  its second. Composition with convex positive (f\) and concave positive
  (L_j\) is therefore convex. These are the required monotonicities;
  convexity of an unrestricted logarithmic product would not suffice.

* For each fixed (j\), the positive finite-plane (L_j\) has a positive
  convex neighborhood of the current compact body. On a smaller compact
  neighborhood the composed convex function has bounded subgradients.
  Its supporting-affine supremum is thus globally finite and agrees on
  the entire current body. No uniform bound in (j\) is required because
  the same separator allows every such test at that fixed (j\).

* With (c=T-\log f>0\), the bounded term
  \(\min(\ell_{j,+},c)\) extends continuously to (L_j=0\), with value
  (c\). This justifies its use against moving boundary and allocated
  cap measures. The reserve comparison holds also on the zero branch:
  \(\ell_{j,+}^2\le c\ell_{j,+}\) there. The remainder is bounded by
  (C\lambda_j\int\ell_{j,+}\), hence vanishes.

* The order of limits is valid: first (j\to\infty\) for fixed (T\),
  then (T\to\infty\) using integrability of the ordinary logarithm.
  Finally replace a nonnegative convex (f\) by (f+\delta\). The result
  is the stated positive-convex inequality
  \(\int\psi f\,d(a+q)\le\beta\int\psi f\,db\).

The scope statement is essential and correct. This order has a possible
mass deficit, so it does not give affine-moment equality or an ordinary
probability martingale. It preserves the actual log-weighted selectors
and does not replace them by closed-cap incidence at the limiting zero
faces. It also permits nonzero defect and supplies no Gamma payment.
